data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ‘emma,’ meaning ‘mother of the earth,’ ‘goddess,’ or ‘rival.’ In the Bible, the name ‘Em’ is not directly used. However, it is a variant of the name ‘Emma,’ which is derived from the Hebrew word ‘ammah,’ meaning ‘mother,’ and is used in the Bible as a name for God and a title for Mary. The name Em carries the meaning “God; Rival” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Em usually hope their child will grow to embody god; rival and live with faith, good character and purpose.
